newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain insists on salary moderation to create jobs.
newsitem.headline: Spain insists on salary moderation to create jobs.

text.p: Spain's Labour Minister Javier Arenas said on Sunday salary moderation was central to achieving the government's objective of job creation in 1997.
Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar declared 1997 "The Year of the Job" in a bid to tame Spain's 22 percent unemployment.

"It is fundamental that salary moderation be maintained in 1997 as it is central to job creation and a general improvement in the job market," Arenas told journalists after a meeting with ministry officials to set out employment objectives for 1997.

The government has acknowledged that extensive reform of Spain's rigid labour market is also needed to achieve greater job creation. It is pressing unions and employers to reach an accord on a series of reforms.
The government has threatened to legislate if an agreement is not reached by early 1997, but Arenas appeared upbeat about the talks on Sunday.
Among objectives for 1997, Arenas said the government would focus on promoting jobs for women, youths, the unemployed over 40 and handicapped people.
The minister said a possible reform of the high cost of dismissals, a key area of rigidity in Spain's labour market, was not on the ministry's agenda for the moment.
"The objective of the government is to facilitate hiring, not firing; to ensure stable, quality jobs," he said.
